Trump Says Putin ‘Certainly Can’ Attend G20 Summit
Trump spoke to reporters at his Florida golf resort, where he was celebrating the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday. He said he did not know whether Putin would come, but he made clear the invitation stands.
“If he wanted to come, he certainly can,” Trump said.

He acknowledged that some people would not want to see Putin at the Dec. 14-15 summit and said he doubted the Russian leader would want to attend. Still, he added, “If it were up to me, I’d like to have him.”
Kremlin Holds Off on Putin G20 Decision

The Kremlin said on Thursday that no decision has been made yet. Putin said after meeting Trump last week that he would consider attending once he had discussed it with the U.S. president. He added that he must first weigh the situation in Russia before traveling to the United States.

Speculation has grown because the Kremlin scheduled Putin’s annual year-end press conference and Direct Line for Dec. 10, earlier than last year’s Dec. 19 event. The earlier date has fueled talk of a possible Miami trip, according to a Pluralia report.
Ukraine War Diplomacy Stays in Focus
Earlier Thursday, Trump said in a Truth Social post that he wants Russia to pull back military aggression across Europe. He said that step could lead to a quick settlement of the war in Ukraine.
